summary: A strong preliminary report: your Great Barrier Reef monitoring concept is well justified with cited literature, and your week-by-week Gantt chart is detailed and mission-linked. Presentation is clean and professional. To lift your mark, add contingency planning to your schedule and, most importantly, show quantitative technical progress — orbit, coverage or link-budget estimates — rather than tutorials and reading alone.
next_steps: Add contingency/slack provision to your Gantt chart (e.g. buffer weeks or alternate task paths) and explain how you would handle project variations.
Produce at least one preliminary technical result: candidate orbit parameters, revisit/coverage analysis, or a first-order link budget, with brief interpretation.
Address the feasibility of near-real-time relay: compare LEO revisit gaps vs GEO coverage for your users' needs.
Convert the 'Useful Links' section into properly formatted, in-text-cited references consistent with your footnoting style.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly states the purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), identifies users (marine and conservation scientists), and justifies need with statistics and four cited sources. Next level: strengthen formal mission goals, objectives and requirements, and discuss orbit/coverage implications of your near-real-time relay claim (LEO revisit gaps vs GEO).
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). Your Gantt chart with weekly tasks and deadlines is detailed and each task is tied to the mission narrative (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end of life). To move higher, add explicit contingency provision for project variations — buffer time or fallback strategies — and show applied course material (orbits, coverage) in the plan.
criteria.C3: Adequate (5/10). Your progress so far is background reading (Asner's Hawaii system, coral bleaching) and STK tutorials 1–4, which shows you are on track but is minor work. The next level requires a good preliminary set of results with description and interpretation — e.g. orbit parameters, coverage analysis, or link budget estimates from STK.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (7/10). Your report has a clear logical structure, consistent formatting, well-written prose, and a labelled Gantt figure with the legend explained in text; footnoted citations match sources. To improve further: cite the 'Useful Links' section in text and format those bare URLs as proper references, and deepen the technical content.
